questions.question: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 650 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 8 km and 10.5 km per hour, respectively. The distance (in metres) between them after 12 minutes is:
questions.questionHtml: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 650 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 8 km and 10.5 km per hour, respectively. The distance (in metres) between them after 12 minutes is:
questions.solution:
Distance traveled by thief in 12 mins = 20/9 × (12 × 60)  = 14400/9 = 1600 m

Distance traveled by police in 12 mins = 17.5/6 × (12 × 60) = 2100 m

Required Distance  = (650 + 1600) - 2100 = 2250 - 2100 = 150 m

questions.question: The price of the X variety of rice is ₹6.95 per kg and the price of the Y variety of rice is ₹5.95 per kg. If the ratio of X variety of rice and Y variety of rice in which it is mixed is 3 : 7, then find the price of the mixed rice (per kg).
questions.questionHtml: The price of the X variety of rice is ₹6.95 per kg and the price of the Y variety of rice is ₹5.95 per kg. If the ratio of X variety of rice and Y variety of rice in which it is mixed is 3 : 7, then find the price of the mixed rice (per kg).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference between Variety X and Variety Y prices = 6.95 − 5.95 = ₹1.00.

Divide this price difference in the inverse ratio parts (Total = 3 + 7 = 10).

Value of 3 parts = (3 ÷ 10) × 1.00 = ₹0.30.

Mixed rice price = Lower price + Shift = 5.95 + 0.30 = ₹6.25.

∴ The correct answer is ₹6.25 per kg.

Alternate Method

Given:

Price of Variety X (P1) = ₹6.95 per kg

Price of Variety Y (P2) = ₹5.95 per kg

Ratio of X to Y (n1 : n2) = 3 : 7

Formula Used:

Mean Price (M) = (n1 × P1 + n2 × P2) ÷ (n1 + n2)

Calculations:

⇒ M = (3 × 6.95 + 7 × 5.95) ÷ (3 + 7)

⇒ M = (20.85 + 41.65) ÷ 10

⇒ M = 62.50 ÷ 10

⇒ M = 6.25

∴ The correct answer is ₹6.25 per kg.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It states that the ratio of the quantities is equal to the ratio of (Higher Price − Mean Price) to (Mean Price − Lower Price).

Weighted Average

When items are mixed in different quantities, the resulting average is the sum of (value × weight) divided by the total weight.

Price vs Quantity Relationship

The mean price always lies between the lowest and the highest individual component prices.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marked his article 150% above the cost price and ratio of discount allowed to profit earned is 4 : 1. If profit earned is Rs.180 less than discount allowed, then find ratio of selling price to marked price of the article
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marked his article 150% above the cost price and ratio of discount allowed to profit earned is 4 : 1. If profit earned is Rs.180 less than discount allowed, then find ratio of selling price to marked price of the article
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Discount (D) to Profit (P) = 4 : 1, and D − P = 180.

⇒ 3 units = 180 ⇒ 1 unit = 60. Thus, P = 60 and D = 240.

Total Markup = P + D = 60 + 240 = 300.

Since Markup is 150% of CP, 1.5 × CP = 300 ⇒ CP = 200.

MP = 200 + 300 = 500 and SP = 200 + 60 = 260.

Ratio SP : MP = 260 : 500 = 13 : 25.

∴ The correct answer is 13 : 25.

Alternate Method

Given:

Markup % = 150% above Cost Price (CP)

Ratio of Discount (D) to Profit (P) = 4 : 1

Difference (D − P) = ₹180

Formula Used:

1. Marked Price (MP) = CP + Markup

2. Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = MP − Discount

3. Markup = Profit + Discount

Calculations:

⇒ Let P = x and D = 4x

⇒ D − P = 180 ⇒ 4x − x = 180

⇒ 3x = 180 ⇒ x = 60

⇒ Profit = ₹60 and Discount = 4 × 60 = ₹240

⇒ Markup = Profit + Discount = 60 + 240 = 300

⇒ 150% of CP = 300 ⇒ (150/100) × CP = 300

⇒ CP = (300 × 100) / 150 = ₹200

⇒ MP = CP + Markup = 200 + 300 = ₹500

⇒ SP = CP + Profit = 200 + 60 = ₹260

⇒ Ratio SP : MP = 260 / 500 = 13 / 25

∴ The correct answer is 13 : 25.

Additional Information

Markup Percentage

It is the percentage by which the cost price is increased to reach the marked price: Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100.

Discount Percentage

It is always calculated on the Marked Price: Discount % = [Discount / MP] × 100.

Relation between CP and MP

A very useful direct ratio is CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

questions.question: In a ∆PQR, X, Y, Z are points on sides PQ, QR, PR such that PX ∶ XQ = 1 ∶ 1, PZ ∶ ZR = 1 ∶ 2, QY ∶ YR = 2 ∶ 3. What is the ratio of the area of quadrilateral XYRZ to that of ∆PXZ?
questions.questionHtml: In a ∆PQR, X, Y, Z are points on sides PQ, QR, PR such that PX ∶ XQ = 1 ∶ 1, PZ ∶ ZR = 1 ∶ 2, QY ∶ YR = 2 ∶ 3. What is the ratio of the area of quadrilateral XYRZ to that of ∆PXZ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the total area of ΔPQR be 30 units (using the LCM of denominator values 6 and 5).

Area of ΔPXZ = (1/2) × (1/3) × 30 = 5 units.

Area of ΔXQY = (1/2) × (2/5) × 30 = 6 units.

Area of quadrilateral XYRZ = Area of ΔPQR − (Area of ΔPXZ + Area of ΔXQY) = 30 − (5 + 6) = 19 units.

Required Ratio = Area of XYRZ ÷ Area of ΔPXZ = 19 / 5.

∴ The correct answer is 19/5.

Alternate Method

Given:

PX : XQ = 1 : 1 ⇒ PX / PQ = 1 / 2 and XQ / PQ = 1 / 2

PZ : ZR = 1 : 2 ⇒ PZ / PR = 1 / 3

QY : YR = 2 : 3 ⇒ QY / QR = 2 / 5

Formula Used:

The ratio of the area of a smaller triangle sharing a vertex with a larger triangle is strictly equal to the product of the fractional length of the sides forming that included angle.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the total area of ΔPQR be A.

⇒ Area of ΔPXZ = (PX / PQ) × (PZ / PR) × A

⇒ Area of ΔPXZ = (1 / 2) × (1 / 3) × A = A / 6

⇒ Area of ΔXQY = (XQ / PQ) × (QY / QR) × A

⇒ Area of ΔXQY = (1 / 2) × (2 / 5) × A = A / 5

⇒ The quadrilateral XYRZ occupies the remaining area of ΔPQR.

⇒ Area of XYRZ = Area(ΔPQR) − [Area(ΔPXZ) + Area(ΔXQY)]

⇒ Area of XYRZ = A − (A / 6 + A / 5)

⇒ Area of XYRZ = A − (11A / 30) = 19A / 30

⇒ Required Ratio = Area(XYRZ) ÷ Area(ΔPXZ)

⇒ Ratio = (19A / 30) ÷ (A / 6)

⇒ Ratio = (19 / 30) × 6 = 19 / 5

∴ The correct answer is 19/5.

Additional Information

Area Proportion by Vertex

When two adjacent triangles share the same vertex and base line, their areas are directly proportional to the lengths of their respective bases since their vertical heights remain identically parallel.

Area Splitting Rule

Any segment intersecting two sides of a given triangle creates a smaller triangular region. Its relative area to the entire triangle is directly derived using: Area(ΔSmall) / Area(ΔLarge) = (Side1 Ratio) × (Side2 Ratio).

Sine Function for Triangles

Area calculation involving side proportionality stems fundamentally from the theorem: Area = (1/2) × a × b × sin(θ). Thus, comparing the respective fractional sides perfectly substitutes finding angular heights.

questions.question: Find the compound interest, if ₹1,60,000 is invested for 2 years at 10% p.a. compounded half yearly
questions.questionHtml: Find the compound interest, if ₹1,60,000 is invested for 2 years at 10% p.a. compounded half yearly
questions.solution:
CI = P[(1 + \(\dfrac{R}{100}\))t - 1]

R = \(\dfrac{R}{2}\) = \(\dfrac{10}{2}\) = 5% and t = 2t = 2 × 2 = 4 years

CI = 160000[(1 + \(\dfrac{5}{100}\))4) - 1] ⇒ CI = 160000[(\(\dfrac{21}{20}\))4 - 1]

CI = 160000 × [\(\dfrac{194481 - 160000}{160000}\)] = 34481

questions.question: A dishonest delivery man purchases 20 liters of pure milk and dilutes it by adding 4 liters of water. If he sells the diluted milk at Rs. 50/L, then what is the cost price of pure milk?
questions.questionHtml: A dishonest delivery man purchases 20 liters of pure milk and dilutes it by adding 4 liters of water. If he sells the diluted milk at Rs. 50/L, then what is the cost price of pure milk?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total quantity of diluted milk = 20 L + 4 L = 24 L.

Total revenue from selling diluted milk = 24 L × Rs. 50/L = Rs. 1200.

To have no profit/loss, total Cost Price of 20 L pure milk must equal the total revenue.

Cost Price of pure milk = 1200 ÷ 20 = Rs. 60/L.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 60/L.

Alternate Method

Given:

Quantity of Pure Milk = 20 L

Quantity of Water Added = 4 L

Selling Price (SP) of diluted milk = Rs. 50/L

Formula Used:

Total Revenue = Total Quantity × Selling Price per unit

Cost Price per unit = Total Cost ÷ Original Quantity

Calculations:

⇒ Total volume of mixture = 20 + 4 = 24 L

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) = 24 × 50 = Rs. 1200

⇒ Since water is free and profit/loss is not mentioned, Total Cost of milk = Total SP

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) of 20 L milk = Rs. 1200

⇒ Cost Price per liter of pure milk = 1200 ÷ 20 = Rs. 60/L

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 60/L.

Additional Information

Profit Percentage in Adulteration

If a milkman sells diluted milk at the Cost Price of pure milk, his profit % is (Quantity of Water ÷ Quantity of Milk) × 100.

Alligation Rule

The ratio of quantities of two ingredients is (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper).

Cost of Water

In mathematical aptitude problems, the Cost Price of water added to milk is always assumed to be zero unless specified otherwise.

questions.question: If \(a=(\sqrt{2}-1)^{\frac{1}{3}}\) , then the value of \(\left(a-\frac{1}{a}\right)^3+3\left(a-\frac{1}{a}\right)\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(a=(\sqrt{2}-1)^{\frac{1}{3}}\), then the value of \(\left(a-\frac{1}{a}\right)^3+3\left(a-\frac{1}{a}\right)\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Recognize the algebraic identity: (x − 1/x)3 + 3(x − 1/x) = x3 − 1/x3.

Given a = (√2 − 1)1/3, cubing both sides gives a3 = √2 − 1.

The reciprocal 1/a3 = 1/(√2 − 1) rationalizes to √2 + 1.

The required value is a3 − 1/a3 = (√2 − 1) − (√2 + 1) = −2.

∴ The correct answer is -2.

Alternate Method

Given: a = (√2 − 1)1/3

Formula Used: (x − y)3 = x3 − y3 − 3xy(x − y)

⇒ a = (√2 − 1)1/3

⇒ Cubing both sides: a3 = √2 − 1

⇒ Let the expression be E = (a − 1/a)3 + 3(a − 1/a)

⇒ Using the expansion of (a − 1/a)3: E = [a3 − 1/a3 − 3(a)(1/a)(a − 1/a)] + 3(a − 1/a)

⇒ E = a3 − 1/a3 − 3(a − 1/a) + 3(a − 1/a)

⇒ E = a3 − 1/a3

⇒ Rationalize 1/a3: 1/(√2 − 1) × (√2 + 1)/(√2 + 1) = (√2 + 1) / (2 − 1) = √2 + 1

⇒ E = (√2 − 1) − (√2 + 1) = √2 − 1 − √2 − 1 = −2

∴ The correct answer is -2.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity

The cubic expansion (x − y)3 = x3 − y3 − 3xy(x − y) is often rearranged to solve for x3 − y3.

Rationalization

To simplify 1/(√x − √y), multiply by the conjugate (√x + √y) to utilize the difference of squares: a2 − b2.

Reciprocal Property

If x = √n − √(n − 1), then its reciprocal is always 1/x = √n + √(n − 1) because the product (√n − √(n − 1))(√n + √(n − 1)) = 1.

questions.question: A train 225 m long is running at a speed of 145 km/hr. What is the time (in seconds) in which it will pass a man who starts from the engine running at the speed of 17 km/hr in the direction opposite to that of the train?
questions.questionHtml: A train 225 m long is running at a speed of 145 km/hr. What is the time (in seconds) in which it will pass a man who starts from the engine running at the speed of 17 km/hr in the direction opposite to that of the train?
questions.solution:
Relative speed of the train in km/h = 145 + 17 ⇒ 162 km/h

Relative speed of the train in m/sec = 162 × 5/18 ⇒ 45 m/sec

According to the concept, the train will cover its own length

So, time = 225/45 ⇒ 5 sec

Time taken by the train to cover the man = 5 sec

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and BC is a diameter of the related circle on which A and D also lie. ∠BCA = 19° and ∠CAD = 32 ° . What is the measure of ∠ACD?
questions.questionHtml: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and BC is a diameter of the related circle on which A and D also lie. ∠BCA = 19° and ∠CAD = 32°. What is the measure of ∠ACD?
questions.solution:
As ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral so, ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°

As BC is the diameter of the circle, so, ∠BAC = 90°

So, ∠BAD = ∠BAC + ∠CAD ⇒ 90° + 32° ⇒ 122°

Now, ∠BCD = 180° - 122° ⇒ 58°

Now, ∠BCD = ∠BCA + ∠ACD ⇒ 58° = 19° + ∠ACD ⇒ ∠ACD = 39°

questions.question: In the given figure, a tangent AC touches the circle (with centre at O) at point B. If ∠DBC = 30 ∘ , then find the value of ∠BOD.
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, a tangent AC touches the circle (with centre at O) at point B. If ∠DBC = 30∘, then find the value of ∠BOD.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The angle subtended by a chord at the centre is twice the angle between the tangent and the chord at the point of contact.

This is derived from the Alternate Segment Theorem combined with the Angle at Centre Theorem.

⇒ ∠BOD = 2 × ∠DBC

⇒ ∠BOD = 2 × 30° = 60°

∴ The correct answer is 60 ^∘.

Alternate Method

Given:

→ AC is a tangent touching the circle at point B.

→ O is the centre of the circle.

→ ∠DBC = 30°

Formula Used:

1. Alternate Segment Theorem: The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

2. Angle at Centre Theorem: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Calculations:

⇒ Let E be a point on the major arc of the circle.

⇒ By Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle in the alternate segment ∠BED = ∠DBC.

⇒ ∠BED = 30°

⇒ By the Angle at Centre Theorem, the angle subtended by arc BD at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.

⇒ ∠BOD = 2 × ∠BED

⇒ ∠BOD = 2 × 30°

⇒ ∠BOD = 60°

∴ The correct answer is 60 ^∘.

Additional Information

Tangent-Radius Property

A tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. Thus, OB ⊥ AC and ∠OBC = 90°.

Isosceles Triangle in Circle

In triangle BOD, OB = OD (radii of the same circle). Therefore, ΔBOD is an isosceles triangle, and ∠OBD = ∠ODB.

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90°).

questions.question: If sec A = \(\frac{15}{7}\) and A + B = 90°, find the value of cosec B.
questions.questionHtml: If sec A = \(\frac{15}{7}\) and A + B = 90°, find the value of cosec B.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given that A + B = 90°, angles A and B are complementary to each other.

According to the complementary angle trigonometric identities, sec A = cosec(90° − A).

Since B = 90° − A, we can substitute this to get sec A = cosec B.

We are given that sec A = 15/7.

Therefore, cosec B is directly equal to 15/7.

∴ The correct answer is 15/7.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ sec A = 15/7

⇒ A + B = 90°

Concept Used:

Consider a right-angled triangle ABC where the two acute angles are A and B. Since their sum is 90°, the third angle C must be exactly 90°.

Calculations:

⇒ In ΔABC right-angled at C, sec A = Hypotenuse ÷ Base adjacent to A

⇒ sec A = AB ÷ AC

⇒ We are given sec A = 15/7, so let the Hypotenuse AB = 15 and Base AC = 7

⇒ We are asked to find the value of cosec B.

⇒ By basic trigonometry, cosec B = Hypotenuse ÷ Perpendicular opposite to B

⇒ Looking at the triangle, the side opposite to angle B is the base AC.

⇒ cosec B = AB ÷ AC

⇒ cosec B = 15/7

∴ The correct answer is 15/7.

Additional Information

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is exactly 90°. In trigonometry, ratios of complementary angles act as co-functions: sin(90°−θ) = cos θ, sec(90°−θ) = cosec θ, and tan(90°−θ) = cot θ.

Basic Trigonometric Ratios

For a right-angled triangle, sec θ is the ratio of the hypotenuse to the adjacent side, while cosec θ is the ratio of the hypotenuse to the opposite side.

Pythagorean Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two legs (a2 + b2 = c2). For the given triangle, BC = √(152 − 72) = √176.

questions.question: What is the probability of getting a pink ball out 3 red, 2 black and 4 pink ball when one ball is drawn at random?
questions.questionHtml: What is the probability of getting a pink ball out 3 red, 2 black and 4 pink ball when one ball is drawn at random?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total outcomes = 3 Red + 2 Black + 4 Pink = 9

Favorable outcomes (Pink balls) = 4

Probability = Favorable Outcomes ÷ Total Outcomes

P(Pink) = 4/9

∴ The correct answer is 4/9.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number of Red balls = 3

Number of Black balls = 2

Number of Pink balls = 4

Formula:

Probability P(E) = n(E) ÷ n(S)

Where n(E) is the number of favorable outcomes and n(S) is the total number of outcomes.

Calculations:

⇒ Total outcomes n(S) = 3 + 2 + 4

⇒ n(S) = 9

⇒ Favorable outcomes for drawing a Pink ball n(E) = 4

⇒ P(Pink) = 4 / 9

∴ The correct answer is 4/9.

Additional Information

Range of Probability

The probability of any event always lies between 0 and 1 (0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1).

Sure and Impossible Events

An impossible event has a probability of 0, while a sure event has a probability of 1.

Complementary Events

The sum of the probability of an event and its complement is 1: P(E) + P(not E) = 1.

questions.question: The difference between the interior angle and the exterior angle of a regular polygon is 60°. The polygon is a ______.
questions.questionHtml: The difference between the interior angle and the exterior angle of a regular polygon is 60°. The polygon is a ______.
questions.solution:
Let the interior angle and exterior angle of the given polygon be x and y respectively,

We know that, x + y = 180º →(1) , And, x - y = 60º →(2)

solve both equations, we get ⇒ x = 120º, y = 60º

Also, the number of sides of the polygon = 360º / y

⇒ number of sides of polygon = 360º / exterior angle = 360º / 60°  = 6

Here, the number of sides in the polygon is 6 which is a Hexagon.

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in a triangle ABC. It touches the sides BC, CA, AB at D, E, F respectively. What is ∠EDF equal to ?
questions.questionHtml: A circle is inscribed in a triangle ABC. It touches the sides BC, CA, AB at D, E, F respectively. What is ∠EDF equal to ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In an Inscribed Circle, the angle formed by the Contact Triangle vertices (like ∠EDF) is directly related to the opposite vertex angle.

The segments from vertices to contact points are equal tangents, creating Isosceles Triangles at each corner: ▵AFE, ▵BDF, and ▵CDE.

Property: The angle subtended by the chord joining two contact points at the third contact point is 90° − (Opposite Angle/2).

For ∠EDF, the opposite vertex is A. ⇒ ∠EDF = 90° − (A/2).

Similarly, ∠DEF = 90° − (B/2) and ∠EFD = 90° − (C/2).

∴ The correct answer is 90° − (A/2).

Alternate Method

Given: A circle is inscribed in ▵ABC touching sides BC, CA, AB at D, E, F respectively.

Formula Used: Alternate Segment Theorem states that the angle between a tangent and a chord is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment.

In ▵ABC, let the internal angles be A, B, and C.

⇒ AF = AE (tangents from external point A are equal).

⇒ In ▵AFE, ∠AFE = ∠AEF.

⇒ ∠A + ∠AFE + ∠AEF = 180°

⇒ ∠A + 2 × ∠AFE = 180°

⇒ ∠AFE = (180° − A) / 2 = 90° − A/2.

⇒ Line AB is a Tangent at point F and FE is a Chord.

⇒ By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between tangent AF and chord FE is equal to the angle subtended by chord FE in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠AFE = ∠EDF.

⇒ ∠EDF = 90° − A/2.

∴ The correct answer is 90° − (A/2).

Additional Information

Incenter and Inradius

The center of the inscribed circle (Incenter) is the intersection of the angle bisectors of the triangle. The inradius r = Area / s, where s is the semi-perimeter.

Tangent Properties

The distance from a vertex to the points of contact is s − a, s − b, and s − c for vertices A, B, and C respectively.

Contact Triangle

The triangle formed by joining the points of contact D, E, and F is called the Gergonne triangle or the Contact triangle of ▵ABC.

questions.question: Find the angle of the sector whose radius is 21 cm and the arc length is 44 cm.
questions.questionHtml: Find the angle of the sector whose radius is 21 cm and the arc length is 44 cm.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Calculate the Circumference of the full circle: 2 × (22/7) × 21 = 132 cm.

The Arc Length is 44 cm, which represents 44/132 = 1/3 of the total Circumference.

The Sector Angle is 1/3 of the full circle angle (360°): 1/3 × 360° = 120°.

∴ The correct answer is 120°.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius (r) = 21 cm

Arc Length (l) = 44 cm

Formula Used:

Arc Length (l) = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

Calculations:

⇒ 44 = (θ ÷ 360) × 2 × (22 ÷ 7) × 21

⇒ 44 = (θ ÷ 360) × 2 × 22 × 3

⇒ 44 = (θ ÷ 360) × 132

⇒ θ = (44 × 360) ÷ 132

⇒ θ = 360 ÷ 3

⇒ θ = 120°

∴ The correct answer is 120°.

Additional Information

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector can be calculated using the formula Area = (θ ÷ 360) × πr2 or Area = (1/2) × r × l.

Perimeter of a Sector

The total boundary length of a sector is given by Perimeter = Arc Length + 2 × Radius.

Radian Measure

If the angle is in radians, the relationship is simply Arc Length (l) = Radius (r) × θ (in radians).

Degree-Radian Conversion

To convert degrees to radians, multiply by π/180. To convert radians to degrees, multiply by 180/π.

questions.question: The population of a country has been growing at a rate of 4% every decade. If the projected population of the country in 2030 is given as 1,58,18,400, what was the population of the country in 2000?
questions.questionHtml: The population of a country has been growing at a rate of 4% every decade. If the projected population of the country in 2030 is given as 1,58,18,400, what was the population of the country in 2000?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Multiplying factor for 4% growth = 1 + (4/100) = 104/100 = 26/25.

Number of decades from 2000 to 2030 is 3, so the total compounding factor is (26/25)3 = 17576/15625.

Initial Population = Final Population × (15625 / 17576)

⇒ Initial Population = 1,58,18,400 × (15625 / 17576)

⇒ Initial Population = 900 × 15625 = 1,40,62,500

∴ The correct answer is 1,40,62,500.

Alternate Method

Given:

Projected population in 2030 (A) = 1,58,18,400

Growth rate (R) = 4% per decade

Time period (n) = (2030 − 2000) ÷ 10 = 3 decades

Formula Used:

A = P × (1 + R/100)n

Where A is the final population, P is the initial population, R is the rate of growth, and n is the time period.

Calculations:

⇒ 1,58,18,400 = P × (1 + 4/100)3

⇒ 1,58,18,400 = P × (104/100)3

⇒ 1,58,18,400 = P × (26/25)3

⇒ P = 1,58,18,400 × (25/26) × (25/26) × (25/26)

⇒ P = 1,58,18,400 × (15625 / 17576)

⇒ P = 900 × 15625

⇒ P = 1,40,62,500

∴ The correct answer is 1,40,62,500.

Additional Information

Compound Population Growth

When a population grows at a constant rate R over a certain period, it increases exponentially in a manner identical to compound interest. The standard formula applied is Final Population = Initial Population × (1 + R/100)n.

Population Depreciation

If the population decreases consistently by a certain percentage R over a period (such as due to mortality or migration), the decay formula becomes Final Population = Initial Population × (1 − R/100)n.

Successive Percentage Change

When the population grows or shrinks at varying rates (R1%, R2%, R3%) in successive time periods, the net final population is calculated as P × (1 ± R1/100) × (1 ± R2/100) × (1 ± R3/100).

questions.question: What is the length of the longest rod that can be placed in a room which is 5 metres long, 12 metres broad and 13 metres high?
questions.questionHtml: What is the length of the longest rod that can be placed in a room which is 5 metres long, 12 metres broad and 13 metres high?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The length of the longest rod in a room is equal to the diagonal of the cuboid.

Diagonal = √(L2 + B2 + H2)

Diagonal = √(52 + 122 + 132) = √(25 + 144 + 169) = √338

Diagonal = √(169 × 2) = 13√2 m

∴ The correct answer is 13√2 metres.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length (L) = 5 m

Breadth (B) = 12 m

Height (H) = 13 m

Formula Used:

Length of longest rod = √(L2 + B2 + H2)

Calculations:

⇒ Square of Length = 52 = 25

⇒ Square of Breadth = 122 = 144

⇒ Square of Height = 132 = 169

⇒ Sum of squares = 25 + 144 + 169

⇒ Sum of squares = 169 + 169 = 338

⇒ Length of rod = √338

⇒ Length of rod = √(169 × 2)

⇒ Length of rod = 13√2 m

∴ The correct answer is 13√2 metres.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total surface area of a room (cuboid) is given by 2(LB + BH + HL).

Volume of Cuboid

The space occupied by the room is calculated as Volume = Length × Breadth × Height.

Diagonal of a Cube

If all sides of the room are equal (a), then the longest rod length = a√3.

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four walls of a room is given by 2H(L + B).

questions.question: 4 \(\frac{4}{5}\) + 2 \(\frac{1}{15}\) - 5 \(\frac{2}{5}\) = 2 \(\frac{1}{5}\) ÷ 3 × k. Find the value of k.
questions.questionHtml: 4\(\frac{4}{5}\) + 2\(\frac{1}{15}\) - 5\(\frac{2}{5}\) = 2\(\frac{1}{5}\) ÷ 3 × k. Find the value of k.
questions.solution:
Given: 

4\(\frac{4}{5}\) + 2\(\frac{1}{15}\) - 5\(\frac{2}{5}\) = 2\(\frac{1}{5}\) ÷ 3 × k

Concept used:

Follow the BODMAS rule according to the table given below:

Calculation:

4\(\frac{4}{5}\) + 2\(\frac{1}{15}\) - 5\(\frac{2}{5}\) = 2\(\frac{1}{5}\) ÷ 3 × k

⇒ 24/5 + 31/15 - 27/5 = 11/5 ÷ 3 × k

⇒ (24 × 3 + 31 - 27 × 3)/15 = 11/15 × k

⇒ (72 + 31 - 81)/15 = 11/15 × k

⇒ 22/15 = 11/15 × k

⇒ k = 22/11 = 2.

Alternate Method

4\(\frac{4}{5}\) + 2\(\frac{1}{15}\) - 5\(\frac{2}{5}\) = 2\(\frac{1}{5}\) ÷ 3 × k

⇒ (4 + 2 - 5) + (4/5 + 1/15 - 2/5) = 11/5 ÷ 3 × k

⇒ 1 + (12 + 1 - 6)/15 = 11/5 ÷ 3 × k

⇒ 1 + 7/15 = 11/5 ÷ 3 × k

⇒ (15 + 7)/15 = 11/15 × k

⇒ 22/15 = 11/15 × k

∴ k = 22/11 = 2.

questions.question: A person invested Rs. 29500 divided into two different schemes A and B at S.I of 12.5% and 15%. If the total amount of the simple interest earned in 2 years is Rs. 8350, What was the amount invested in scheme A. (In Rs.)
questions.questionHtml: A person invested Rs. 29500 divided into two different schemes A and B at S.I of 12.5% and 15%. If the total amount of the simple interest earned in 2 years is Rs. 8350, What was the amount invested in scheme A. (In Rs.)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total interest for 1 year = 8350 ÷ 2 = ₹4175.

Assume total ₹29500 was invested in Scheme B at 15%.

Calculated interest = 29500 × 15% = ₹4425.

Difference in interest = 4425 − 4175 = ₹250.

Amount in Scheme A = Difference ÷ (Rate B − Rate A) = 250 ÷ (15% − 12.5%) = 250 ÷ 2.5% = ₹10000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹10000.

Alternate Method

Given: Total Investment = ₹29500, Rate A = 12.5%, Rate B = 15%, Total Interest (2 yrs) = ₹8350.

Formula Used: Simple Interest (S.I.) = (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

⇒ Interest if all amount in Scheme A for 2 years = (29500 × 12.5 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹7375

⇒ Interest if all amount in Scheme B for 2 years = (29500 × 15 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹8850

⇒ Total actual interest earned = ₹8350

⇒ By Alligation Method, Ratio of Investment (A : B) = (8850 − 8350) : (8350 − 7375)

⇒ Ratio A : B = 500 : 975 = 20 : 39

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 20 + 39 = 59 units

⇒ 59 units = ₹29500 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹500

⇒ Amount in Scheme A = 20 × 500 = ₹10000

∴ The correct answer is ₹10000.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Concept

Simple Interest is calculated only on the Principal amount. Formula: S.I. = P × R × T ÷ 100.

Alligation in Interest

When a sum is divided into two parts at different rates, the Alligation of the interest rates or interests gives the ratio of the Principals.

Effective Rate of Interest

Overall Rate % = (Total Interest ÷ Total Principal) × (100 ÷ Time). This helps find the weighted average of multiple schemes.

questions.question: The average of Virat in the last 5 innings was found to be 55.6 after taking into consideration that he got out in all of the innings. But later on, it was found that Virat remained not out in one of the innings. Find the correct average.
questions.questionHtml: The average of Virat in the last 5 innings was found to be 55.6 after taking into consideration that he got out in all of the innings. But later on, it was found that Virat remained not out in one of the innings. Find the correct average.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total runs scored = Average × Assumed Outs = 55.6 × 5 = 278.

Correct number of outs = Total Innings − Not Out innings = 5 − 1 = 4.

Correct Batting Average = Total Runs ÷ Correct Outs = 278 ÷ 4 = 69.5.

∴ The correct answer is 69.5.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial average of Virat = 55.6, Number of innings = 5, Initial assumed outs = 5, Actual Not Out innings = 1.

Formula Used: Batting Average = Total Runs ÷ (Total Innings − Not Out Innings)

⇒ Total runs = Initial Average × Number of innings

⇒ Total runs = 55.6 × 5 = 278

⇒ Correct number of innings where he got out = 5 − 1 = 4

⇒ Correct Average = 278 ÷ 4

⇒ Correct Average = 69.5

∴ The correct answer is 69.5.

Additional Information

Batting Average Definition

In cricket, the batting average is calculated by dividing the total runs scored by the number of times the batsman got out, not simply the number of innings played.

Handling Not Out Innings

If a player remains Not Out in an inning, that inning is added to the total matches but it does not increment the divisor used to calculate the average.

Sum of Observations

The sum of any set of values is equal to the Average × Total count of observations. Formula: Sum = Avg × n.

questions.question: The value of an Apple laptop depreciated from Rs. 1,33,100 to Rs. 72,900 in 3 years. Find the yearly rate of depreciation. (Correct to 2 decimal places.)
questions.questionHtml: The value of an Apple laptop depreciated from Rs. 1,33,100 to Rs. 72,900 in 3 years. Find the yearly rate of depreciation. (Correct to 2 decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Final Value to Initial Value = 72900 ÷ 133100 = 729 ÷ 1331

For a period of 3 years, take the cube root of the ratio: 3√(729) ÷ 3√(1331) = 9 ÷ 11

This means the value of the laptop drops from 11 parts to 9 parts in one year.

Yearly Depreciation % = [(11 − 9) ÷ 11] × 100 = (2 ÷ 11) × 100

Depreciation % = 18.18%

∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Value (P) = Rs. 1,33,100

Final Value (A) = Rs. 72,900

Time (n) = 3 years

Formula Used:

A = P × (1 − R/100)n

Calculations:

⇒ 72900 = 133100 × (1 − R/100)3

⇒ 72900 ÷ 133100 = (1 − R/100)3

⇒ 729 ÷ 1331 = (1 − R/100)3

⇒ (9 ÷ 11)3 = (1 − R/100)3

⇒ 9 ÷ 11 = 1 − R/100

⇒ R/100 = 1 − (9 ÷ 11)

⇒ R/100 = 2 ÷ 11

⇒ R = 200 ÷ 11

⇒ R = 18.1818... ≈ 18.18%

∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.

Additional Information

Depreciation Formula

Depreciation represents a consistent percentage decrease over time and follows the compound interest formula with a negative rate: A = P(1 − R/100)n.

Appreciation Formula

When an asset's value increases annually (like population growth), use the standard compound interest formula: A = P(1 + R/100)n.

Effective Rate of Successive Depreciation

For two consecutive years with the same depreciation rate R, the net effective depreciation percentage is given by: 2R − R2/100.

questions.question: P and Q take part in 400 m race. P runs at 12 km/hr. P gives Q a start of 20 m and still beats him by 13 seconds. The speed of Q is: (Round up to two decimal places.)
questions.questionHtml: P and Q take part in 400 m race. P runs at 12 km/hr. P gives Q a start of 20 m and still beats him by 13 seconds. The speed of Q is: (Round up to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed of P in m/s = 12 × (5/18) = 10/3 m/s.

Time taken by P to finish the race = 400 ÷ (10/3) = 120 seconds.

Time taken by Q = 120 + 13 = 133 seconds.

Distance run by Q = 400 − 20 = 380 m.

Speed of Q = 380 ÷ 133 = 20/7 m/s ⇒ (20/7) × (18/5) = 72/7 = 10.29 km/hr.

∴ The correct answer is 10.29 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total distance of race = 400 m

Speed of P = 12 km/hr

Start distance given to Q = 20 m

Time by which P beats Q = 13 seconds

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed conversion: 1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s

Calculations:

⇒ Speed of P = 12 × (5/18) = 10/3 m/s

⇒ Time taken by P to complete the race = 400 ÷ (10/3) = 120 seconds

⇒ P gives Q a start of 20 m, so distance covered by Q = 400 − 20 = 380 m

⇒ P beats Q by 13 seconds, so Time taken by Q = Time taken by P + 13

⇒ Time taken by Q = 120 + 13 = 133 seconds

⇒ Speed of Q in m/s = Distance ÷ Time = 380 ÷ 133 = 20/7 m/s

⇒ Speed of Q in km/hr = (20/7) × (18/5) = 72/7 km/hr

⇒ Speed of Q ≈ 10.2857 km/hr

⇒ Rounding up to two decimal places, Speed of Q = 10.29 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 10.29 km/hr.

Additional Information

Start Distance in Races

If A gives B a start of x meters in a race of L meters, it means A has to run the complete L meters while B only has to run (L − x) meters.

Start Time in Races

If A beats B by t seconds, it implies B takes t seconds more than A to complete his designated track distance.

Speed Conversions

To convert km/hr into m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s into km/hr, multiply the value by 18/5.

questions.question: The distance between the centres of two circles touching externally is 12 cm. If the sum of their areas is 104π cm 2 , then the radius of the larger circle is
questions.questionHtml: The distance between the centres of two circles touching externally is 12 cm. If the sum of their areas is 104π cm2, then the radius of the larger circle is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two circles touch externally, the distance between their centres is the sum of their radii: r1 + r2 = 12.

Sum of areas = π(r12 + r22) = 104π ⇒ r12 + r22 = 104.

Test values from 12 that satisfy r12 + r22 = 104: Pairs (11,1), (10,2), (9,3), (8,4), (7,5).

Checking (10, 2): 102 + 22 = 100 + 4 = 104. This matches the given condition.

The larger radius is therefore 10 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.

Alternate Method

Let the radii of the two circles be r1 and r2 cm.

Given: distance between centres = 12 cm (External touch)

⇒ r1 + r2 = 12 — (i)

Given: Sum of areas = 104π cm2

⇒ πr12 + πr22 = 104π

⇒ r12 + r22 = 104 — (ii)

We know that (r1 + r2)2 = r12 + r22 + 2r1r2

⇒ 122 = 104 + 2r1r2

⇒ 144 − 104 = 2r1r2

⇒ 40 = 2r1r2 ⇒ r1r2 = 20

Solving for r using x2 − (Sum)x + (Product) = 0:

⇒ x2 − 12x + 20 = 0

⇒ x2 − 10x − 2x + 20 = 0

⇒ (x − 10)(x − 2) = 0

⇒ x = 10 cm or x = 2 cm

The radius of the larger circle is 10 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.

Additional Information

Circles Touching Externally

When two circles of radii r1 and r2 touch externally, the distance between their centres is equal to r1 + r2.

Circles Touching Internally

When two circles touch internally, the distance between their centres is the absolute difference of their radii, |r1 − r2|.

Area of a Circle

The area of a circle with radius r is given by A = πr2. The sum of areas of two circles is π(r12 + r22).

questions.question: If \(\left(\mathrm{x}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)=2 \sqrt{3}\) , what is the value of \(\left(\mathrm{x}^3+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)~\) , given that x is a positive number?
questions.questionHtml: If \(\left(\mathrm{x}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)=2 \sqrt{3}\), what is the value of \(\left(\mathrm{x}^3+\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)~\), given that x is a positive number?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If x − 1/x = a, then (x + 1/x)2 = a2 + 4.

Substituting a = 2√3 ⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = (2√3)2 + 4 = 12 + 4 = 16.

Since x is a positive number, x + 1/x = 4.

Now, if x + 1/x = k, then x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k.

For k = 4, x3 + 1/x3 = 43 − 3(4) = 64 − 12 = 52.

∴ The correct answer is 52.

Alternate Method

Given:

x − 1/x = 2√3

Formulas Used:

1) (x + 1/x)2 = (x − 1/x)2 + 4

2) x3 + 1/x3 = (x + 1/x)3 − 3(x + 1/x)

Calculations:

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = (2√3)2 + 4

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = (22 × 3) + 4

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = 12 + 4 = 16

⇒ x + 1/x = √16 = 4 (as x is positive)

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 43 − 3 × 4

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 64 − 12

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 52

∴ The correct answer is 52.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity for x2 + 1/x2

If x + 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 − 2. If x − 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 + 2.

Identity for x3 − 1/x3

If x − 1/x = k, then x3 − 1/x3 = k3 + 3k. This is derived from the expansion of (x − 1/x)3.

Relation between Sum and Difference

The expressions (x + 1/x)2 and (x − 1/x)2 differ exactly by 4, as (x + 1/x)2 − (x − 1/x)2 = 4.

questions.question: A container has 20% milk and 80% water in it. It is mixed with another sample (in equal quantity) having 80% milk and 20% water. What would be the milk content in the final mixture?
questions.questionHtml: A container has 20% milk and 80% water in it. It is mixed with another sample (in equal quantity) having 80% milk and 20% water. What would be the milk content in the final mixture?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two mixtures are mixed in equal quantities, the concentration of a component in the final mixture is the arithmetic mean of its concentrations in the individual samples.

Final Milk content = (Milk% in Sample 1 + Milk% in Sample 2) ÷ 2

⇒ Final Milk content = (20% + 80%) ÷ 2

⇒ Final Milk content = 100% ÷ 2 = 50%

∴ The correct answer is 50%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Milk in Container 1 = 20%

Milk in Container 2 = 80%

Mixing ratio = 1 : 1 (Equal quantity)

Using the Rule of Alligation:

⇒ (80 − M) ÷ (M − 20) = 1 ÷ 1

⇒ 80 − M = M − 20

⇒ 2M = 100

⇒ M = 50

∴ The correct answer is 50%.

Additional Information

Weighted Average Formula

When quantities n1 and n2 are mixed with concentrations c1 and c2, the average M = (n1c1 + n2c2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Rule of Alligation

It is a rule that enables us to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at the given price must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired price.

Percentage Concentration

In any mixture, the sum of the percentages of all individual components (like milk and water) always equals 100%.

questions.question: The graphs of the equations 3x + y – 5 = 0 and 2x – y – 5 = 0 intersect at the point P(α, β). What is the value of (3 α + β)?
questions.questionHtml: The graphs of the equations 3x + y – 5 = 0 and 2x – y – 5 = 0 intersect at the point P(α, β). What is the value of (3 α + β)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The intersection point P(α, β) lies on both given linear equations.

By property, any point on the line satisfies the equation of that line.

Substitute x = α and y = β into the first equation: 3x + y − 5 = 0.

⇒ 3α + β − 5 = 0

⇒ 3α + β = 5

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation 1: 3x + y = 5

Equation 2: 2x − y = 5

Solving for P(α, β):

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate y:

⇒ (3x + y) + (2x − y) = 5 + 5

⇒ 5x = 10

⇒ x = 2

So, the x-coordinate (α) is 2.

Now, substitute x = 2 in Equation 2:

⇒ 2(2) − y = 5

⇒ 4 − y = 5

⇒ y = −1

So, the y-coordinate (β) is −1.

Calculation:

We need to find (3α + β):

⇒ 3(2) + (−1)

⇒ 6 − 1 = 5

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information

Point of Intersection

The coordinates of the intersection point of two graphs satisfy both equations simultaneously.

System of Linear Equations

A system has a unique solution if the lines are intersecting, no solution if they are parallel, and infinite solutions if they are coincident.

Algebraic Methods

Common methods to find P(x, y) include substitution, elimination, and Cramer's rule using determinants.

questions.question: A tank when full can be emptied by an outlet pipe A in 5.6 hours, while an inlet pipe B can fill the same empty tank in 7 hours. If pipes A and B are turned on alternatively for 1 hour each starting with pipe A when the tank is full, how long will it take to empty the tank?
questions.questionHtml: A tank when full can be emptied by an outlet pipe A in 5.6 hours, while an inlet pipe B can fill the same empty tank in 7 hours. If pipes A and B are turned on alternatively for 1 hour each starting with pipe A when the tank is full, how long will it take to empty the tank?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total capacity = LCM(5.6, 7) = 28 units.

Efficiency: Pipe A = +5 units/hr (emptying), Pipe B = −4 units/hr (filling).

Net work in 1 cycle (2 hours) = 5 − 4 = 1 unit emptied.

Safe zone before Pipe A's final turn = 28 − 5 = 23 units.

Time for 23 units = 23 × 2 = 46 hours, remaining 5 units emptied by A in 1 hour.

∴ The correct answer is 47 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by outlet pipe A to empty the tank = 5.6 hours.

Time taken by inlet pipe B to fill the tank = 7 hours.

Pipes are opened alternatively for 1 hour each, starting with A.

Calculations:

Pipe Hours Total Work Efficiency
Pipe A 5.6 28 5
Pipe B 7 −4

⇒ Let emptying the tank be positive work (+), and filling be negative work (−).

⇒ Work done in the 1st hour by A = 5 units.

⇒ Work done in the 2nd hour by B = −4 units.

⇒ Total work done in 1 cycle (2 hours) = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

⇒ Since A can empty 5 units in its turn, we calculate full cycles for 28 − 5 = 23 units.

⇒ Time required to empty 23 units = 23 cycles × 2 hours/cycle = 46 hours.

⇒ Remaining work = 28 − 23 = 5 units.

⇒ In the 47th hour, Pipe A will empty the remaining 5 units in exactly 1 hour.

⇒ Total time taken = 46 + 1 = 47 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 47 hours.

Additional Information

Pipes and Cisterns

Inlet pipes add to the volume (+ efficiency) and outlet pipes remove volume (− efficiency). The total work is assumed as the LCM of the given time periods.

Alternate Work Concept

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shringara Rasa during the spring season.

Key Points

  • The 'Daph' dance is a traditional folk dance performed with a circular wooden drum known as Daphli. It is an integral part of various Indian cultural celebrations.
  • This dance is primarily associated with expressing joy and romance during the spring season, which aligns with the Shringara Rasa.
  • Shringara Rasa is one of the nine Rasas (emotions) in Indian aesthetics and symbolizes love, beauty, and attraction. It is highly celebrated in art and culture, including music, dance, and literature.
  • Spring season is considered the season of renewal and romance, which makes the 'Daph' dance a perfect cultural expression of these emotions.
  • The rhythmic beats of the Daphli, combined with graceful movements and vibrant attire, create an atmosphere of joy, celebration, and harmony.

Additional Information

  • Rasas in Indian Aesthetics:
    • The concept of Rasa originates from ancient Indian texts like the Natyashastra by Bharata Muni.
    • There are nine Rasas: Shringara (Romantic), Hasya (Humor), Karuna (Compassion), Raudra (Anger), Veera (Courage), Bhayanaka (Fear), Bibhatsa (Disgust), Adbhuta (Wonder), and Shanta (Peace).
    • Shringara Rasa is often depicted through vibrant colors, joyful expressions, and fluid movements in art and performance.
  • Significance of Spring Season:
    • Spring is considered the season of renewal and growth, symbolizing new beginnings and rejuvenation.
    • It is celebrated across cultures with festivals, dances, and rituals, often highlighting themes of love, nature, and harmony.
    • In India, the festival of Holi, which celebrates colors and joy, is often associated with the spring season.
  • Daphli as a Musical Instrument:
    • The Daphli is a circular wooden drum with a membrane stretched over it, played by striking or tapping.
    • It is widely used in folk music and dances across India, contributing to rhythmic and melodic expressions.
    • Its portability and ease of play make it popular among performers during cultural events and festivals.
  • Other Seasonal Dances in India:
    • Bihu Dance: Celebrated in Assam during the spring season to mark the Assamese New Year.
    • Ghoomar Dance: Performed in Rajasthan during special occasions, including spring festivals.
    • Chhau Dance: A tribal dance from Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal, performed during seasonal transitions.

Important Points

  • Incorrect Options:
    • Mourning during a funeral: The 'Daph' dance is a celebratory dance, and mourning is not its theme. Hence, this is incorrect.
    • Martial valor during warfare: The dance does not depict courage or valor; it is associated with joy and romance. This is incorrect.
    • Deep meditation in monsoons: The 'Daph' dance is lively and vibrant, contrasting the calmness of meditation. Hence, this is incorrect.
  • Cultural Context:
    • The 'Daph' dance is an example of how Indian folk traditions celebrate emotions and seasons through artistic expressions.
    • It reflects the deep connection between nature, human emotions, and cultural heritage.

questions.question: Under the Punjab Reorganisation Act 1966, which committee was primarily responsible for demarcating the boundaries of Haryana and Punjab?
questions.questionHtml: Under the Punjab Reorganisation Act 1966, which committee was primarily responsible for demarcating the boundaries of Haryana and Punjab?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is J.C. Shah Commission.

Key Points

  • The Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 was enacted by the Indian Parliament to divide the state of Punjab and create the new state of Haryana, along with reorganizing the union territory of Chandigarh.
  • The J.C. Shah Commission, chaired by Justice J.C. Shah, was primarily responsible for the demarcation of boundaries between Punjab and Haryana under this Act.
  • The commission used various criteria such as geographical, linguistic, cultural, and administrative factors to determine the separation and allocation of territories.
  • Chandigarh was declared a shared capital for both Punjab and Haryana and was retained as a union territory under the Act.
  • The recommendations of the J.C. Shah Commission led to significant changes in the territorial structure of Punjab, including the formation of Haryana on 1st November 1966.
  • The division was aimed at addressing linguistic and regional differences that had arisen due to the demand for a separate state by Hindi-speaking people in Punjab. 

Additional Information

  • Fazal Ali Commission:
    • The Fazal Ali Commission, also known as the States Reorganisation Commission, was established in 1953 to reorganize states based on linguistic lines.
    • Its recommendations led to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, which created states like Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Maharashtra.
    • The commission’s focus was on linguistic and cultural factors, but it did not handle the Punjab-Haryana division directly.
    • Hence, this option is incorrect for the question.
  • Sarkaria Commission:
    • The Sarkaria Commission was constituted in 1983 to examine the relationship between the central and state governments.
    • Its focus was administrative and financial relations, not territorial reorganization.
    • Hence, this option is irrelevant for the Punjab-Haryana division.
  • Dhar Commission:
    • The Dhar Commission, set up in 1948, was tasked with investigating the feasibility of states’ reorganization on administrative grounds.
    • It recommended reorganization based on administrative convenience rather than linguistic lines.
    • The recommendations of this commission were rejected in favor of the linguistic criteria proposed by the Fazal Ali Commission.
    • Hence, this option is not applicable.
  • Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966:
    • This act led to the division of Punjab into two states: Punjab and Haryana, and the union territory of Chandigarh.
    • It addressed the long-standing demand for a separate state for Hindi-speaking populations in Punjab.
    • The act also reassigned certain territories to Himachal Pradesh.
    • The J.C. Shah Commission played a pivotal role in implementing the provisions of this act.

Important Points

  • Criteria for Reorganization:
    • The separation of Punjab and Haryana was based on linguistic differences, with Punjabi-speaking areas retained in Punjab and Hindi-speaking areas forming Haryana.
    • Administrative convenience and geographical factors were also considered in the demarcation process.
  • Implications of the Reorganization:
    • The reorganization addressed regional demands but also led to disputes over shared resources, including water and the status of Chandigarh.
    • It set a precedent for other territorial reorganizations in India.

questions.questionHtml:
Match the following correctly.
List – I List – II
1. Partition of Bengal a. 1909
2. Separate electorates b. 1915
3. Lucknow Pact c. 1905
4. Formation of Hindu Mahasabha d. 1916

Code :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1-c, 2-a, 3-d, 4-b.

Key Points

  • Partition of Bengal (1905):
    • The partition of Bengal was announced on July 19, 1905, by the then Viceroy of India, Lord Curzon, and it was implemented on October 16, 1905.
    • The British claimed the reason was administrative convenience, but the actual objective was to divide the center of Indian nationalism and create a rift between Hindus and Muslims.
    • This event triggered the Swadeshi Movement and the Boycott Movement across the country.
  • Separate Electorates (1909):
    • Separate electorates were introduced through the Indian Councils Act of 1909, popularly known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.
    • Under this system, Muslims were given the right to elect their own representatives in designated constituencies, effectively recognizing communalism in the Indian political structure.
    • This policy was a significant step in the British "divide and rule" strategy.
  • Lucknow Pact (1916):
    • The Lucknow Pact was an agreement reached between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League at their joint session held in Lucknow in December 1916.
    • The session was presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar and marked the reunion of the Moderates and Extremists within the Congress.
    • Both parties agreed to demand self-government from the British and accepted the principle of separate electorates for Muslims in provincial legislatures.
  • Formation of Hindu Mahasabha (1915):
    • The Akhil Bharatiya Hindu Mahasabha was established in 1915 during the Kumbh Mela at Haridwar.
    • It was founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya and other prominent leaders to protect the rights and interests of the Hindu community.
    • The organization was formed in response to the political developments of the time, including the formation of the Muslim League in 1906.

Additional Information

  • Lord Curzon's Reactionary Policies: Lord Curzon served as the Viceroy from 1899 to 1905. Apart from the Partition of Bengal, he passed the Official Secrets Act (1904) and the Indian Universities Act (1904), both of which were seen as attempts to curb Indian nationalism.
  • The Morley-Minto Reforms: Named after Lord Morley (Secretary of State) and Lord Minto (Viceroy). Lord Minto is often referred to as the "Father of Communal Electorate" in India due to the 1909 reforms.
  • Annulment of Partition: Due to persistent protests and the rise of revolutionary activities, the Partition of Bengal was eventually annulled in 1911 by Lord Hardinge during the Delhi Durbar.
  • Home Rule Movement: Around the time of the Lucknow Pact in 1916, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant launched the Home Rule League to advocate for Dominion Status for India.
  • Significant Arrival: The year 1915 is also highly significant in Indian history because Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on January 9, a date now celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

Important Points

  • Evolution of Commmualism: The Shimla Deputation of 1906 led by the Aga Khan paved the way for the 1909 separate electorates, which significantly altered the course of Indian independence.
  • Surat Split (1907): The internal conflict regarding the method of protest against the 1905 partition led to the Surat Split in 1907, where Congress divided into Extremists (led by Lal-Bal-Pal) and Moderates (led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale).
  • Significance of 1916: The Lucknow Pact is considered a peak period of Hindu-Muslim unity in the Indian freedom struggle, facilitated largely by the efforts of Tilak and Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

  • While Tilak was known for his aggressive stance and support for revolutionary spirit, he primarily focused on mass mobilization and passive resistance (such as Boycott and Swadeshi) rather than advocating for a complete armed revolution as the sole methodology. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
  • Tilak’s ideology was rooted in national unity and cultural pride; he did not emphasize communal representation. In fact, he was a key architect of the Lucknow Pact in 1916, which aimed at Hindu-Muslim unity to demand self-government. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
  • The Extremist leaders, including Tilak, believed that political freedom (Swaraj) must precede economic reforms or social changes, arguing that without the power to govern, meaningful economic progress was impossible. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
  • Tilak used tools like National Education and mass agitation to instill a sense of pride and demand for Swaraj among the common people, shifting the movement from the elite classes to the masses.

Additional Information

  • The Extremist Phase (1905–1919): This period was characterized by a more radical approach to the Indian National Congress, led by the trio Lal-Bal-Pal (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal). They grew disillusioned with the Moderate methods of "Prayer, Petition, and Protest" after the Partition of Bengal in 1905.
  • Literary Contributions: Tilak used his newspapers, Kesari (in Marathi) and The Mahratta (in English), to spread nationalist ideas and criticize British policies. He also wrote the Gita Rahasya while imprisoned in Mandalay Jail, Burma, between 1908 and 1914.
  • Cultural Mobilization: To bridge the gap between the Congress and the common people, Tilak transformed traditional festivals into political platforms. He started the Ganpati Festival in 1893 and the Shivaji Festival in 1895 to foster national spirit and unity.
  • Home Rule Movement: In April 1916, Tilak launched the Indian Home Rule League at Belgaum. His league operated in Maharashtra (excluding Bombay), Karnataka, Central Provinces, and Berar, demanding self-government within the British Empire.

Important Points

  • The Surat Split (1907): The ideological difference between the Moderates and Extremists led to a formal split in the Indian National Congress during the Surat Session. The Extremists, led by Tilak, wanted to extend the Swadeshi movement nationwide, while Moderates wanted to confine it to Bengal.
  • Father of Indian Unrest: British colonial authorities, specifically Valentine Chirol, described Bal Gangadhar Tilak as the "Father of Indian Unrest" due to his influence in inciting anti-British sentiment.
  • Anti-Liquor and No-Tax Campaigns: Tilak organized No-Tax campaigns in Maharashtra during the famine of 1896-97 and was a staunch advocate of Prohibition (anti-liquor movements) to improve the socio-economic condition of the poor.
  • Legacy: Tilak's death on August 1, 1920, coincided with the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement by Mahatma Gandhi, marking a transition from the Extremist phase to the Gandhian Era of the national struggle.

questions.question: With reference to the Round Table Conferences (1930–1932) held in London, consider the following statements: I. The announcement of the Communal Award in 1932 followed the inability of the conferences to produce a mutually acceptable agreement on minority representation. Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.questionHtml:
With reference to the Round Table Conferences (1930–1932) held in London, consider the following statements:

I. Mahatma Gandhi participated in more than one Round Table Conference and represented the Indian National Congress in those deliberations.

II. The announcement of the Communal Award in 1932 followed the inability of the conferences to produce a mutually acceptable agreement on minority representation.

Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option A.

 

Key Points

  • The Round Table Conferences were a series of three meetings held in London between representatives of the British Government, Indian political leaders, and princely states to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
  • Mahatma Gandhi participated only in the Second Round Table Conference (1931) as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress. He did not participate in more than one conference. Hence, Statement I is incorrect.
  • The Round Table Conferences failed to reach a consensus on minority representation, particularly regarding separate electorates for various communities. Following this deadlock, the British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award, which extended separate electorates to several minority groups. Hence, Statement II is correct.
  • Since the question asks which statement is incorrect, only Statement I is incorrect → Option A.

Additional Information

  • The First Round Table Conference (1930) was attended by princes, liberals, and minority representatives, but the Congress boycotted it.
  • The Second Round Table Conference (1931) included Gandhi as the Congress representative, but disagreements over minority representation prevented progress.
  • The Third Round Table Conference (1932) was poorly attended by Indian leaders and produced limited outcomes.
  • The Communal Award (1932) granted separate electorates to minorities including Muslims, Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans, and the Depressed Classes, leading to strong opposition from Gandhi and the eventual Poona Pact.

questions.question: With reference to the Doctrine of Merger in the Indian judicial system, which one of the following best describes its meaning?
questions.questionHtml: With reference to the Doctrine of Merger in the Indian judicial system, which one of the following best describes its meaning?

options.text: The principle by which civil and criminal courts are brought under a common judicial structure
options.html: The principle by which civil and criminal courts are brought under a common judicial structure

options.text: The absorption of a subordinate court’s decision into the judgment or order of a superior court
options.html: The absorption of a subordinate court’s decision into the judgment or order of a superior court

options.text: The doctrine under which international treaty obligations prevail over judicial decisions
options.html: The doctrine under which international treaty obligations prevail over judicial decisions

options.text: The incorporation of a legislative enactment into judicial interpretation
options.html: The incorporation of a legislative enactment into judicial interpretation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.

Key Points

  • Doctrine of Merger is a judicial principle based on the hierarchy of courts and tribunals. It means that when a superior court modifies, reverses or affirms the order of a subordinate court, tribunal or authority in appeal or revision, the subordinate forum’s decision merges into the decision of the superior forum. Thereafter, the superior court’s order is the operative and enforceable order in law.
  • Option A: The Doctrine of Merger does not mean bringing civil and criminal courts under a common judicial structure. Hence, A is incorrect.
  • Option B: The doctrine means the absorption of a subordinate court’s decision into the judgment or order of a superior court when the superior court decides the matter in appeal or revision. Hence, B is correct.
  • Option C: It is not related to international treaty obligations prevailing over judicial decisions. Hence, C is incorrect.
  • Option D: It does not mean incorporation of a legislative enactment into judicial interpretation. Hence, D is incorrect.
  • Therefore, the Doctrine of Merger is best described as the absorption of a subordinate court’s decision into the judgment or order of a superior court.

Additional Information

  • Core idea: There cannot be two operative orders governing the same matter at the same time. Once the superior court passes its order, the lower court’s order loses its independent operative identity.
  • When it applies: It generally applies when a superior court exercises appellate or revisional jurisdiction and affirms, modifies or reverses the lower forum’s order.
  • Important distinction: The doctrine is not about merging courts or jurisdictions. It is about the legal effect of a superior court’s decision on the order of a subordinate forum.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, which specific Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency under Article 359?
questions.questionHtml: According to the Constitution of India, which specific Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency under Article 359?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Articles 20 and 21.

Key Points
  • Article 359 of the Constitution of India empowers the President to suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights during a National Emergency.
  • The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 introduced a significant restriction on this power, stating that the enforcement of the rights guaranteed by Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during an emergency. Hence, the correct answer is Articles 20 and 21.
  • Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offences, which includes protection against ex-post-facto laws, double jeopardy, and self-incrimination. Hence, this statement ensures legal safeguards for individuals.
  • Article 21 guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty, declaring that no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law. Hence, this statement protects the most fundamental human right.
  • Articles 14 and 15 (Right to Equality) can be suspended by a Presidential Order under Article 359. Hence, option 1 is incorrect.
  • Article 19 (Six Freedoms) is automatically suspended under Article 358 when an emergency is declared on grounds of war or external aggression. Hence, option 2 is incorrect.
  • Article 22 (Protection against arrest and detention) is not exempted from suspension under Article 359. Hence, option 3 is incorrect.
Additional Information
  • Article 352 of the Indian Constitution allows the President to declare a National Emergency when the security of India is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
  • Article 358 deals with the suspension of Fundamental Rights guaranteed by Article 19. This suspension is automatic and does not require a separate Presidential Order, but it only applies when the emergency is declared due to war or external aggression.
  • The 44th Amendment Act was passed in 1978 by the Janata Government led by Morarji Desai to prevent the recurrence of the civil liberty violations seen during the 1975 Emergency.
  • A National Emergency must be approved by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha within one month from the date of its issue by a special majority.
  • The Presidential Order under Article 359 can specify the period for which the enforcement of certain rights is suspended and the territorial extent (whole or part of India) of such suspension.
Important Points
  • In the landmark ADM Jabalpur vs Shivkant Shukla (1976) case, also known as the Habeas Corpus case, the Supreme Court had controversially ruled that even the right to life under Article 21 could be suspended during an emergency. This ruling was effectively nullified by the 44th Amendment.
  • India has experienced three National Emergencies: the first in 1962 (Indo-China war), the second in 1971 (Indo-Pak war), and the third in 1975 (internal disturbance).
  • The 44th Amendment also replaced the vague term internal disturbance with armed rebellion as a ground for declaring a National Emergency under Article 352.
  • While the enforcement of rights is suspended, the Fundamental Rights themselves are not deleted from the Constitution; they remain valid but the remedy to approach the court for their violation is temporarily blocked.

questions.question: Match List-I (Disease) with List-II (Causative Agent): List-I List-II (i) Tuberculosis (a) Virus (ii) Malaria (b) Bacteria (iii) AIDS (c) Fungi (iv) Ringworm (d) Protozoa
questions.questionHtml:
Match List-I (Disease) with List-II (Causative Agent):
List-I List-II
(i) Tuberculosis (a) Virus
(ii) Malaria (b) Bacteria
(iii) AIDS (c) Fungi
(iv) Ringworm (d) Protozoa
questions.solution:
The correct answer is (i)-b, (ii)-d, (iii)-a, (iv)-c.

Key Points

  • Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease matched with Bacteria. It is specifically caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily targets the lungs but can affect other parts of the body. Hence, statement (i)-b is correct.
  • Malaria is matched with Protozoa. It is caused by single-celled microorganisms of the Plasmodium group. This parasite is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. Hence, statement (ii)-d is correct.
  • AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) is matched with Virus. It is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), which attacks the body's immune system, specifically the CD4 cells (T cells). Hence, statement (iii)-a is correct.
  • Ringworm is matched with Fungi. Despite its name, it is not caused by a worm but by a fungal infection of the skin. Common genera of fungi responsible for this include Trichophyton, Microsporum, and Epidermophyton. Hence, statement (iv)-c is correct.
  • By analyzing the matches, Option 1 provides the only sequence where every disease is correctly paired with its specific causative agent.

Additional Information

  • Bacterial Diseases: Bacteria are single-celled prokaryotic organisms. Other examples of bacterial diseases include Cholera (caused by Vibrio cholerae), Typhoid (caused by Salmonella typhi), and Anthrax. Most bacterial infections are treated using antibiotics, which were first discovered in 1928 by Alexander Fleming.
  • Viral Diseases: Viruses are microscopic parasites, much smaller than bacteria, that lack the capacity to thrive and reproduce outside of a host body. Common viral diseases include Influenza, Common Cold, Hepatitis B, and COVID-19. Unlike bacteria, viruses do not respond to antibiotics; instead, vaccines and antiviral drugs are used for prevention and treatment.
  • Protozoan Diseases: Protozoa are unicellular eukaryotes. Besides Malaria, other notable diseases include Amoebic Dysentery (caused by Entamoeba histolytica) and Sleeping Sickness (caused by Trypanosoma). These often involve vectors like flies or mosquitoes for transmission.
  • Fungal Diseases: Fungi are eukaryotic organisms that include yeasts and molds. Skin diseases like Athlete's foot and Ringworm are contagious and spread through direct contact or by sharing personal items like towels and clothes in humid locations.

Important Points

  • Diagnostic Tests: For AIDS, the ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) test is widely used for initial screening, followed by the Western Blot test for confirmation. For Tuberculosis, the Mantoux tuberculin skin test or Sputum Smear microscopy is used.
  • Prevention and Vaccination: The BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guérin) vaccine is administered globally to protect children against Tuberculosis. While there is no widely available vaccine for all types of Malaria, the RTS,S/AS01 vaccine was recently recommended by the WHO in 2021 for children in areas with moderate to high transmission.
  • Global Impact: According to World Health Organization (WHO) reports, Tuberculosis remains one of the top 10 causes of death worldwide. Malaria caused an estimated 249 million cases in 2022 across 85 countries, with the majority of the burden in the African Region.
  • Mode of Transmission: Understanding the causative agent is vital for public health. Viral and bacterial diseases are often airborne or waterborne, whereas protozoan diseases frequently require a biological vector, and fungal diseases are predominantly topical or contact-based.

questions.question: What condition is sometimes referred to as "Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi"?
questions.questionHtml: What condition is sometimes referred to as "Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Typhoid.

Key Points

  • Typhoid fever is a life-threatening systemic infection caused by the bacterium Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi. It is a human-specific pathogen, meaning it is only carried and transmitted by humans.
  • The disease is primarily characterized by a sustained high fever that can reach as high as 39° to 40° C (103° to 104° F). Other common symptoms include weakness, stomach pain, headache, and loss of appetite.
  • Transmission of the Salmonella Typhi bacteria occurs via the fecal-oral route. This usually happens when an individual consumes contaminated food or water that has been handled by an infected person or a chronic carrier who sheds the bacteria in their feces.
  • In some patients, a rash consisting of small, flat, rose-colored spots may appear on the chest or abdomen. If left untreated, the infection can lead to severe intestinal perforation or internal hemorrhaging, which can be fatal.
  • A famous historical example of a carrier is Mary Mallon, popularly known as "Typhoid Mary," who was an asymptomatic carrier in New York during the early 1900s and unintentionally infected many people while working as a cook.

Additional Information

  • Malaria: This is a disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, which are transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. It is not caused by Salmonella but is common in tropical and subtropical regions.
  • Yellow Fever: It is an acute viral hemorrhagic disease transmitted by infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. It is characterized by jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes), and it is most prevalent in parts of Africa and South America.
  • Diarrhoea: This is a condition defined by the passage of three or more loose or liquid stools per day. While it is a symptom of Typhoid, it can be caused by various other agents including viruses like Rotavirus or bacteria like Vibrio cholerae and Escherichia coli.
  • Diagnosis: The most common diagnostic tool for Typhoid in many developing nations is the Widal test, which detects antibodies against the O and H antigens of Salmonella Typhi.
  • Prevention: Prevention strategies include vaccination (such as the Vi conjugate vaccine), improving sanitation, and ensuring access to safe drinking water.

Important Points

  • The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that there are between 11 and 21 million cases of typhoid fever annually, with the highest burden seen in South-East Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Modern treatment involves the use of antibiotics such as Ciprofloxacin, Azithromycin, or Ceftriaxone. However, there is increasing global concern regarding Extensively Drug-Resistant (XDR) typhoid strains that do not respond to standard treatments.
  • Salmonella Typhi lives only in humans. Unlike other Salmonella strains (like those causing food poisoning), it cannot be caught from animals.
  • The incubation period for the disease usually ranges from 6 to 30 days, after which the symptoms begin to manifest gradually.

Key Points

  • The 38th National Games of India are scheduled to be hosted by the state of Uttarakhand. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) has confirmed the inclusion of various traditional and modern sports disciplines for this edition.
  • Traditional sports like Yoga and Mallakhamb have been integrated into the official roster of the National Games to promote Indigenous sports culture in India. These sports were also highlight features in the previous 37th edition held in Goa.
  • The inclusion of these sports aims to provide a platform for athletes practicing traditional Indian disciplines to showcase their talent at a national level. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
  • Regarding the second statement, while Uttarakhand is known for its adventure sports and white-water rafting, there is no official record of a world record being set specifically within the 38th National Games competition through a nighttime river rafting event.
  • Although promotional events or trials for Night Rafting have been conducted in regions like Rishikesh on the Ganges river to boost tourism and celebrate the spirit of the games, they are not categorized as a competitive medal event that set a world record during the games' official proceedings. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
  • Hence, the correct answer is Only 1.

Additional Information

  • The 38th National Games:
    • The 38th edition of the National Games is slated to take place in Uttarakhand in late 2024 or early 2025. The event will see participation from thousands of athletes across all States and Union Territories of India.
    • The Official Mascot and logo for the games often reflect the local biodiversity and culture of the host state, which in this case includes the Himalayan heritage.
  • The National Games of India:
    • The National Games are organized by the Indian Olympic Association (IOA). The first edition was held in 1924 in Lahore (undivided India) as the Indian Olympic Games.
    • The main objective is to identify and nurture sporting talent for international events like the Olympics and Asian Games.
    • Mallakhamb, a traditional Indian sport where a gymnast performs aerial yoga or gymnastic postures on a vertical wooden pole, originated in Maharashtra and has gained immense popularity nationwide.
    • Yoga was officially added as a competitive sport in the National Games to align with the global recognition of the International Day of Yoga (celebrated on June 21).

Important Points

  • Host State Details: Uttarakhand will utilize venues in cities like Dehradun, Haldwani, and Rishikesh for various events. The state government has invested heavily in upgrading infrastructure, including the Maharana Pratap Sports College.
  • Historical Context: The 37th National Games were held in Goa in 2023, where Maharashtra topped the medal tally, winning the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about the scheme of Jan Shikshan Sansthan of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT correct about the scheme of Jan Shikshan Sansthan of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)?

options.text: It focuses on creation of a pool of master trainers
options.html: It focuses on creation of a pool of master trainers

options.text: It is implemented through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs)
options.html: It is implemented through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs)

options.text: It focuses to improve the occupational skills and technical knowledge of the non/neo literates and persons having rudimentary level of education
options.html: It focuses to improve the occupational skills and technical knowledge of the non/neo literates and persons having rudimentary level of education

options.text: It focuses on identifying and promoting traditional skills in the districts through skilling/upskilling
options.html: It focuses on identifying and promoting traditional skills in the districts through skilling/upskilling

questions.solution:
The correct answer is It is implemented through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs).

Key Points

  • Statement 1: The Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) scheme emphasizes the creation of a pool of master trainers and resource persons who are skilled in specific vocations to provide training at the grassroots level. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
  • Statement 2: The JSS scheme is not implemented through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs); instead, it is implemented through Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and voluntary agencies registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
  • Statement 3: The primary objective of the scheme is to improve the occupational skills and technical knowledge of non-literates, neo-literates, and persons with a rudimentary level of education (up to 8th standard) and school dropouts (up to 12th standard). Hence, statement 3 is correct.
  • Statement 4: The scheme focuses on identifying and promoting traditional skills in the districts through skilling and upskilling, ensuring that local heritage and indigenous crafts provide livelihood opportunities. Hence, statement 4 is correct.
  • The Jan Shikshan Sansthan scheme is a unique initiative that aims to provide vocational training in a non-formal mode to the marginalized sections of society.

Additional Information

  • Historical Background: The scheme was initially launched as Shramik Vidyapeeth in the year 1967 in Mumbai. It was later renamed Jan Shikshan Sansthan in the year 2000.
  • Institutional Transfer: The scheme was previously under the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD), but it was transferred to the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) in July 2018 to better align vocational training with market demands.
  • Target Demographics: The priority group for JSS includes women, Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), minorities, and other economically weaker sections. The age group of the target beneficiaries is usually 15 to 45 years.
  • Geographical Reach: There are approximately 301 functional Jan Shikshan Sansthans spread across various districts in India, serving both rural and urban slum areas.
  • Course Varieties: The training includes a wide range of trades such as cutting and tailoring, beauty culture and health care, electrical technician, soft toys making, and handicrafts.

Important Points

  • Funding Structure: JSS is a 100% Central Sector Scheme. The Government of India provides an annual recurring grant to the NGOs for infrastructure, staff salaries, and training expenses.
  • Certification: Trainees receive a certificate upon successful completion of the course, which is often validated by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET), improving their chances for self-employment or wage employment.
  • Digital Literacy: In recent years, the MSDE has integrated digital literacy and life skills into the JSS curriculum to ensure that beneficiaries can navigate the modern digital economy and access government schemes.
  • Impact and Monitoring: The performance of each Sansthan is monitored through a dedicated JSS Portal, which tracks enrollment, training progress, and placement data of the candidates.
