  • Initially, it was a 100% Centrally Sponsored Scheme. However, following the recommendations of the 14th Finance Commission, the funding pattern was modified to a ratio of 60:40 between the Centre and States (and 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States).
  • The Ministry of Rural Development is the nodal ministry responsible for the implementation and monitoring of this nationwide plan. The scheme targets habitations with a population of 500 and above in plain areas and 250 and above in hilly, tribal, and desert areas.
  • It specifically focuses on constructing all-weather roads, which include necessary culverts and cross-drainage structures that are operable throughout the year, including the monsoon season.

Additional Information

  • Swaranjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY):
    • Launched in April 1999, this was a holistic program covering all aspects of self-employment such as organization of the poor into Self Help Groups (SHGs), training, credit, and marketing.

  • Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY):
    • This scheme was launched on 1st December 1997 to provide gainful employment to the unemployed and underemployed urban poor.
    • It focused on encouraging self-employment and provision of wage employment, specifically within urban local bodies.
  • Bharatmala Pariyojana:
    • Launched in 2017, this is a centrally-sponsored and funded Road and Highways project of the Government of India.
    • It focuses on optimizing the efficiency of freight and passenger movement across the country by bridging critical infrastructure gaps through Economic Corridors, Inter-corridors, and Feeder Routes.
  • Rural Connectivity and Poverty Alleviation:
    • Increased connectivity directly impacts the Human Development Index (HDI) of a region by improving the reach of healthcare workers and educational facilities to remote villages.
    • Studies indicate that for every 1 crore rupees invested in rural roads, a significant number of people are lifted above the poverty line due to improved market linkages.

Important Points

  • PMGSY Phase-II: Launched in May 2013, this phase focused on the up-gradation of 50,000 km of the existing Rural Road Network to improve overall efficiency.
  • PMGSY Phase-III: Approved in 2019, it involves consolidation of 1,25,000 km through Routes and Major Rural Links that connect habitations to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), Higher Secondary Schools, and Hospitals.
  • Technological Integration: The government uses the OMMAS (Online Management, Monitoring and Accounting System) GIS system to track the progress of road construction and ensure transparency.
  • Use of Waste Material: Under PMGSY, there is a push for using Green Technology and non-conventional materials like Waste Plastic, Cold Mix Technology, and Fly Ash in road construction to promote environmental sustainability.

questions.question: Which scientific reason explains why convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in motor vehicles?
questions.questionHtml: Which scientific reason explains why convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in motor vehicles?

options.text: They provide a wider field of view by forming diminished and erect images
options.html: They provide a wider field of view by forming diminished and erect images

options.text: They produce real and inverted images to help drivers estimate distance
options.html: They produce real and inverted images to help drivers estimate distance

options.text: They magnify distant objects to make them appear larger and closer
options.html: They magnify distant objects to make them appear larger and closer

options.text: They polarize incoming light to reduce the intensity of headlight glare
options.html: They polarize incoming light to reduce the intensity of headlight glare

questions.solution:
The correct answer is They provide a wider field of view by forming diminished and erect images.

Key Points

  • A convex mirror, also known as a diverging mirror, is a curved mirror in which the reflective surface bulges toward the light source.
  • It is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles because it always forms an erect (upright) and diminished (smaller) image of the objects behind the vehicle. This allows the driver to see a much larger area than a plane mirror would allow. Hence, statement A is correct.
  • Convex mirrors cannot produce real and inverted images; they only produce virtual images because the reflected rays appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror. Hence, statement B is incorrect.
  • These mirrors do not magnify objects; rather, they reduce the size of the image to compress a wider field of view into the limited surface area of the mirror. Hence, statement C is incorrect.
  • The reduction of headlight glare is typically managed through polarizing filters or electrochromic technology in modern mirrors, not by the basic geometric curvature of a standard convex mirror. Hence, statement D is incorrect.

Additional Information

  • Mirror Formula: The mathematical relationship between the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) is expressed as 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. For a convex mirror, the focal length is always considered positive because the focus lies behind the mirror.
  • Magnification (m): It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object (m = h'/h = -v/u). In the case of a convex mirror, the magnification is always positive and less than 1, signifying that the image is virtual, erect, and smaller.
  • Applications: Apart from motor vehicles, these mirrors are used in ATM security to allow users to see what is happening behind them, in supermarkets for surveillance, and on sharp road curves (blind spots) to prevent accidents by showing oncoming traffic.
  • Geometrical Features: The center of curvature and the principal focus of a convex mirror are situated behind the reflecting surface. This geometry causes parallel rays of light to diverge upon reflection.

Important Points

  • Safety Warning: Most rear-view mirrors in India and the USA contain the warning text: "Objects in the mirror are closer than they appear." This is because the diminished size of the image can lead the driver's brain to underestimate the proximity of the trailing vehicle.
  • Comparison with Concave Mirrors: A concave mirror is a converging mirror that can form both real and virtual images. It is used as a shaving mirror or by dentists because it can produce a magnified image when the object is placed very close to it.
  • Reflective Properties: The laws of reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) apply to spherical mirrors just as they do to plane mirrors, but the normal at the point of incidence always passes through the center of curvature (C).

questions.question: The unit of electric flux is represented by which quantity derived from the product of electric field and surface area?
questions.questionHtml: The unit of electric flux is represented by which quantity derived from the product of electric field and surface area?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Newton m2 per coulomb.

Key Points

  • Electric Flux is defined as the total number of electric field lines passing through a given surface area in a unit of time.
  • It is a scalar quantity that describes the strength and distribution of the electric field over a surface.
  • The mathematical formula for electric flux is the product of the electric field (E) and the component of the area (A) perpendicular to the field: \( \Phi_E = E \cdot A \cdot \cos\theta \).
  • The SI unit of the electric field is Newton per coulomb (N/C).
  • The SI unit of surface area is square meters (m2).
  • By multiplying the units of the electric field and area, the resulting unit of electric flux is (Newton/Coulomb) × square meters, which is Newton m2 per coulomb.
  • The unit can also be represented as Newton m2 C−1.

Additional Information

  • Weber: This is the SI unit of magnetic flux, not electric flux. It is equivalent to one Tesla-square meter.
  • Tesla: This is the SI unit of magnetic field strength or magnetic flux density.
  • Joule: This is the SI unit of energy or work, defined as the work done by a force of one Newton over a displacement of one meter.
  • Volt-meter: Since the electric field can also be measured in Volts per meter (V/m), electric flux can alternatively be expressed in Volt-meters (V × m).
  • The dimensional formula for electric flux is [ML3T−3A−1].

questions.question: Which of the following is a moderator commonly used in nuclear reactors?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a moderator commonly used in nuclear reactors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - All of the above

Key Points

  • Nuclear Moderator
    • A moderator is a material used in a nuclear reactor to slow down fast neutrons produced during fission.
    • Slow-moving neutrons, known as thermal neutrons, are more likely to cause further fission in Uranium-235 nuclei, sustaining the chain reaction.
    • Commonly used moderators include:
      • Graphite: Used in many early reactors and modern gas-cooled reactors.
      • Water (Light Water): The most widely used moderator in commercial power plants (PWR and BWR).
      • Heavy Water (Deuterium Oxide): Used in reactors like CANDU because of its low neutron absorption.

Additional Information

  • Heavy Water (D₂O)
    • Consists of deuterium (an isotope of hydrogen) instead of regular hydrogen.
    • It is highly efficient because it has a very low neutron absorption cross-section, meaning it slows neutrons without capturing them.
  • Graphite
    • Graphite is a form of carbon that possesses high thermal stability and good moderating properties.
    • It was used as the moderator in the world's first artificial nuclear reactor, Chicago Pile-1.
  • Control Rods vs. Moderators
    • While moderators slow down neutrons, control rods are designed to absorb neutrons to regulate or stop the reaction.
    • Materials like Boron and Cadmium are commonly used for control rods.
  • Coolants
    • A coolant carries away the heat generated by the fission reaction to produce steam.
    • In many reactors, water or heavy water serves the dual purpose of both moderator and coolant.

questions.question: Which is the primary source of helium on Earth, accumulating in natural gas deposits as a result of nuclear decay processes over millions of years?
questions.questionHtml: Which is the primary source of helium on Earth, accumulating in natural gas deposits as a result of nuclear decay processes over millions of years?

options.text: Radioactive decay of uranium and thorium

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Radioactive decay of uranium and thorium

Key Points
  • The primary source of helium-4 on Earth is the alpha decay of heavy radioactive elements, specifically uranium and thorium, found in the Earth's crust.
  • During the process of radioactive decay, these heavy nuclei emit alpha particles, which are essentially helium nuclei consisting of two protons and two neutrons.
  • Over millions of years, these alpha particles capture electrons from their surroundings to become stable helium atoms.
  • Because helium is a non-reactive noble gas, it migrates through the crust and becomes trapped in impermeable rock formations, often accumulating in the same reservoirs as natural gas (methane).
  • Photosynthesis is incorrect as it is a biological process that produces oxygen and glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
  • Cosmic rays interact with the upper atmosphere to produce small amounts of helium-3 and tritium, but they are not the source of the vast underground helium deposits used commercially.
  • Mantle convection refers to the physical movement of the Earth's mantle due to heat, which helps transport gases but is not the nuclear process that generates helium.
Additional Information
  • Helium is the second most abundant element in the observable universe, but it is relatively rare on Earth because it is light enough to escape Earth's gravity and leak into space.
  • Most of the world's commercial helium is extracted through fractional distillation of natural gas, where helium concentrations can reach up to 7 percent.
  • The United States, Qatar, and Algeria are among the top global producers of helium.
  • Helium is critical for high-tech applications, including cooling superconducting magnets in MRI scanners, manufacturing semiconductors, and as a lifting gas for balloons and airships.
  • Because it is produced over geological timescales (millions of years) and escapes into space once released, helium is considered a non-renewable resource.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is (i) - True, (ii) - True.

Key Points

  • Statement (i) about CD-R is true. A CD-R is a Write Once-Read Many (WORM) disk. It means that once the data has been written onto the disc, it can't be modified or deleted but it can be read multiple times.
  • Statement (ii) about CD-RW is also true. CD-RW allows data to be written, erased, and re-written. It's a type of rewritable disc that permits multiple write cycles.

questions.question: _________ translates a low level language program into Machine Code
questions.questionHtml: _________ translates a low level language program into Machine Code
questions.solution:

Key Points

  • An assembler is a program that translates assembly language code into machine code.
  • Assembly language is a low-level programming language that is closely related to machine code but is more readable for humans.
  • Assembly language uses mnemonics for operations and addresses, making it easier to program than binary machine code.
  • The machine code output by the assembler can be directly executed by the computer's CPU.
  • Assemblers are crucial for programming embedded systems and other low-level hardware components.

 Additional Information

  • Compiler
    • A compiler translates high-level programming languages (like C, C++, or Java) into machine code.
    • Unlike assemblers, compilers deal with more abstract and complex code structures.
    • Compilers perform various optimization techniques to make the code run efficiently.
  • Interpreter
    • An interpreter executes instructions written in a programming or scripting language directly, without needing them to be compiled into machine code first.
    • Languages like Python and JavaScript often use interpreters.
    • Interpreters are generally slower than compiled programs because they translate code on-the-fly.
  • Virus
    • A computer virus is a type of malicious software that, when executed, replicates by inserting copies of itself into other computer programs, data files, or the boot sector of the hard drive.
    • Viruses often cause harmful effects, such as corrupting data or taking control of the system.
    • They are not related to the process of translating programming languages.

questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for loading operating system from secondary memory to primary memory ?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is responsible for loading operating system from secondary memory to primary memory ?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Bootstrap loader.

Key Points

  • The bootstrap loader, often simply called the "boot loader," is a small program that is responsible for loading the operating system (OS) from secondary memory (such as a hard drive or SSD) into primary memory (RAM).
  • A bootstrap loader is a program in the computer's firmware or ROM that initiates the operating system when the computer is turned on. It loads the initial code needed to start the OS, initializing hardware, memory, and other system components.
  • Upon powering on, the bootstrap loader (part of BIOS or UEFI) activates. It locates the OS's boot loader, typically on the hard drive or external storage, loads it into memory, and transfers control to it, enabling the OS to start.

Additional Information

  • CPU: The CPU executes instructions but does not handle the specific task of loading the OS from secondary to primary memory.
  • Power on self test (POST): The POST is responsible for checking hardware components during the initial startup but does not load the OS.
  • Boot record: The boot record contains the information about where the OS is located on the disk but does not itself load the OS into memory.

questions.question: One Kilobyte is equivalent to ________ nibbles.

    • Bits are usually assembled into a group of eight to form a byte.

questions.question: In Windows OS, which of the following actions will permanently delete a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin?
questions.questionHtml: In Windows OS, which of the following actions will permanently delete a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Press Shift + Delete.

Key Points

  • Pressing Shift + Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin and permanently deletes a file from the system.
  • This action removes the file from the file system table, making it inaccessible to the user unless recovery methods are employed.
  • The Recycle Bin is a feature in Windows OS that stores deleted files temporarily until manually cleared.
  • Files deleted using Shift + Delete cannot be restored through the Recycle Bin.
  • For accidental permanent deletion, specialized data recovery software may be required to retrieve the file.

Additional Information

  • Recycle Bin in Windows OS
    • The Recycle Bin is a special folder where deleted files are temporarily stored.
    • Users can restore files from the Recycle Bin unless the bin has been emptied or files are deleted permanently using Shift + Delete.
    • The Recycle Bin can be customized to allocate a specific amount of storage space for deleted files.
  • Permanent Deletion
    • Permanent deletion bypasses temporary storage locations like the Recycle Bin.
    • It removes file references from the file system, but the actual data remains on the storage device until overwritten.
    • Tools like disk shredders can be used to overwrite deleted files, ensuring complete erasure.
  • Data Recovery
    • Data recovery tools like EaseUS or Recuva can retrieve files that have been deleted permanently, provided the data has not been overwritten.
    • Recovery is more successful if attempted promptly after deletion.
  • Keyboard Shortcuts in Windows
    • Shift + Delete: Permanently deletes a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin.
    • Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V: Copy and paste files or content.
    • Alt + Tab: Switch between open windows.
    • Ctrl + Z: Undo the last action.

questions.question: Amritya Veena is planning to connect 15 computers of her training center using Ethernet Cable. Which one of the following devices should she use for the same?

questions.question: A temporary storage area, attached to the CPU, for Input / Output operations, is called as ______.
questions.questionHtml: A temporary storage area, attached to the CPU, for Input / Output operations, is called as ______.

questions.question: Which of the following MS-Excel functions returns a number rounded up, away from zero, to the nearest multiple of significance?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following MS-Excel functions returns a number rounded up, away from zero, to the nearest multiple of significance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is CEILING( )

Key Points

  • CEILING(): This function rounds a number up, away from zero, to the nearest multiple of significance.
  • The "significance" represents the multiple to which you want to round the number.
  • For example, if you have a number like 4.1 and you wanted to round up to the nearest whole number, you would use CEILING(4.1, 1) and it would return 5.

Additional Information

  • ROUND(): This Excel function round off numbers to a specified number of digits. It follows the standard rules of rounding numbers. If the next digit to the specified number of digits is 5 or above, it rounds up; if it's less than 5, it rounds down. For example, ROUND(2.15, 1) would return 2.2.
  • CELL(): This function in Excel is used to get information about the formatting, location, or contents of a particular cell. It doesn't round numbers. It has two parts, first is the info-type e.g. address, row, col, etc. which represents what information you want to fetch and the second is optional, which refers to the reference cell.
  • FLOOR(): Similar to the CEILING function, the FLOOR function in Excel rounds a number down (towards zero), to the nearest multiple of significance. For example, FLOOR(4.7, 1) would return 4.

Remember, both the FLOOR and CEILING functions will round towards or away from zero (negative values inclusive), respectively. For rounding strictly down or up (ignoring zero), Excel uses FLOOR.MATH and CEILING.MATH.
